units: <cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 2:1">Meg. II, 1</cite> <he>הקורא … למ׳</he> he who reads the Book of Esther in an irregular way (corresp. to <he>סירוסין</he>, ib. 18ᵇ top). Ib. 17ᵃ (ref. to <cite ref="Esther 9:27">Esth. IX, 27</cite>) <he>מה זמנם למ׳ לא אף כתבם למ׳ לא</he> as you cannot disregard the order of these days in celebrating their season, so you must not transpose the order in which the events of these days are described.

<cite ref="Esther 9:27">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Esther 9:28">Esth. IX, 28</cite>) <he>מה עשייה למ׳ לא אף זכירה למ׳ לא</he> as you cannot subvert the celebration, so you must not subvert the order of recitation.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 27a:2">Snh. 27ᵃ</cite> <he>למ׳ הוא נפסל</he> he becomes disqualified as witness retroactively, i.e. his testimonies are invalidated from the time that he perjured himself (opp. <he>מיכן ולהבא</he>, v. <cite ref="B00007"><he>בָּא</he> III</cite>).

<cite ref="Eruvin 37b">Erub. 37ᵇ</cite>, sq … <he>ונמצא … למ׳</he> and the retroactive result would be that he drank untithed wine at the time; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 7:4:3">Y. Dem. VII, 26ᵇ</cite> <he>למִפְרֵעוֹ</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 3:8:4">Y. Gitt. III, end, 45ᵇ</cite> <he>למפרעו הוא נעשה חומץ</he> is it to be considered as sour wine at the time, i.e. from the day that he was bound to examine it? <cite ref="Tosefta Sotah 11:9">Tosef. Sot. XI, 9</cite> <he>מְנֵה … למ׳</he> count thirty-three days backward.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 49">Gen. R. s. 49</cite> <he>חזור בך למ׳</he> take up the argument going back gradually (from fifty to forty-five &c.); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Tosefta Berakhot 4:19">Tosef. Ber. IV, 19</cite>, sq. <he>לברך למ׳</he> to say the blessing after meal, opp. <he>כתחלה</he>(<he>ל</he>); <cite ref="Pesachim 101b">Pes. 101ᵇ</cite>
